source_notice: Argentina / ARS Evidence Closure (from-scratch). Material public claims are rebuilt from current primary BCRA, ARCA/Dirección General de Aduanas, UIF and Boletín Oficial / argentina.gob.ar normativa sources. The BCRA monetary regime is pinned to flotación cambiaria dentro de bandas (from 11 April 2025; from 1 January 2026 band-edge drift uses INDEC inflation T-2). Border cash is pinned to ARCA Resolución General 5659/2025 as the controlling legal text (inbound ≥ USD 10,000 declaration; outbound foreign cash/instruments/minted precious metals physical carriage only when total < USD 10,000; ARS outbound ≥ USD 10,000-equivalent via OM 2250-B declaration). Resident FX purchase/holding, outward-transfer overlays and business concept paths incorporate the Exterior y Cambios official summary, Comunicación A 8226, the Texto Ordenado baseline through A 8307 (25 August 2025), and the material post-A 8307 CAMEX effects relevant to the governed fields — A 8332 (initial 3.8.5 insider securities-settlement undertaking), A 8336 (3.8.5 extended en todos los casos), and A 8417 (including point 7 / 3.14.1 outward-transfer registration and securities DJ, plus concept-specific export/services/deadline/debt adjustments). Comunicación A 8441 (SECOEXPO / CNV foreign-currency pagaré application) was reviewed as a current-corpus CAMEX communication and is not mapped to a governed field because argentina.json does not assert a matching claim. Exact final section/page/article pinning and cross-document locator refinement remain for Pinpoint Hardening. Dólar blue / parallel unofficial rates are excluded from the exchange-rate regime claim. Argentina remains unpublished and candidate_only pending separate Pinpoint Hardening and Publication Closure.
country_overview: Argentina's currency is the Argentine peso (ARS). The Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA) administers monetary and foreign-exchange regulation under the Mercado Libre de Cambios framework (Decree 260/02 as amended) and its Exterior y Cambios texto ordenado plus complementary CAMEX communications. Since 11 April 2025 the BCRA operates a floating exchange-rate regime within administered moving bands (flotación cambiaria dentro de bandas): inside the band the rate is market-determined by supply and demand, with BCRA boundary/intervention mechanics at the edges; from 1 January 2026 the monthly drift of both edges is determined by the latest INDEC monthly inflation figure with a two-month lag (T-2). That monetary-regime fact is kept analytically separate from layered exchange controls and transaction-specific FX-access and surrender rules under Exterior y Cambios. Passenger physical carriage of cash, bearer negotiable instruments and minted precious metals is administered by ARCA / Dirección General de Aduanas under Resolución General 5659/2025, with AML information flows to the Unidad de Información Financiera (UIF). Parallel unofficial market labels such as the dólar blue are not treated here as the official exchange-rate regime.

summary.traveler: Argentina does not have one symmetric USD 10,000 cash figure. Under ARCA RG 5659/2025, inbound travellers/crew must declare cash, bearer negotiable instruments (foreign or ARS) and/or minted precious metals when the total is equal to or greater than USD 10,000 equivalent (≥) on form OM 2249-A — a declaration trigger, not an import ceiling. Outbound foreign-currency cash, foreign-currency bearer instruments and minted precious metals may leave as baggage/pacotilla only when the total is strictly below USD 10,000; at or above that amount, foreign currency/instruments must exit through entities authorised by the Superintendencia de Entidades Financieras y Cambiarias, not by ordinary traveller declaration alone. Outbound ARS cash and ARS bearer instruments at or above USD 10,000 equivalent follow a separate OM 2250-B customs declaration path. Amounts are per traveller; under-16 non-emancipated minors apply 50% of the stated figures; a transit exception exists where the inbound OM 2249-A was completed.
summary.business: FX transactions must be conducted through an authorised FX entity at a freely agreed rate, with documentation sufficient to establish genuineness and correct concept classification under the BCRA Exterior y Cambios framework. Export proceeds of goods and services are, as a general rule, subject to surrender/liquidation in the FX market within BCRA-set deadlines, while resident access for imports, services, dividends, financial debt and similar concepts remains concept-specific. Non-resident FX purchases/repatriations may require prior BCRA conformity except for enumerated exceptions. Current-account and capital operations are not described here as simply unrestricted.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Under ARCA Resolución General 5659/2025 Art. 1, travellers of any category and crew who bring into Argentine territory as baggage or pacotilla cash, bearer negotiable instruments (in foreign currency or legal-tender ARS) and/or minted precious metals must declare them to Customs on form OM 2249-A when the total value is equal to or greater than the equivalent of USD 10,000 (U$S 10.000) — operator igual o superior / ≥, using the Banco de la Nación Argentina buyer rate of the prior business day. This is a declaration trigger, not a quantitative import ceiling: amounts above the threshold may enter if declared. Information registered in the Sistema Ingreso y Egreso de Valores is supplied to the UIF. Transit passengers who declared on entry under Art. 9 may exit under that declaration when presented at the exit customs office.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Outbound physical carriage is asymmetric with inbound declaration. RG 5659/2025 Art. 2 permits travellers/crew to leave as baggage/pacotilla with foreign-currency cash, foreign-currency bearer negotiable instruments and/or minted precious metals only when the total value is inferior to USD 10,000 (or equivalent) — strictly <, seller rate of the prior business day. Art. 3 provides that when the total is equal to or greater than that Art. 2 amount, foreign currency and foreign-currency bearer instruments may leave Argentine territory only through entities authorised by the Superintendencia de Entidades Financieras y Cambiarias. Separately, Art. 4 allows outbound ARS legal-tender cash and ARS-issued bearer instruments at or above the USD 10,000 equivalent to leave via customs declaration on form OM 2250-B. Arts. 2–4 are per person; under-16 non-emancipated minors use 50% figures (Art. 5). This architecture is not a single symmetric 'declaration at USD 10,000' rule and is not an ordinary outbound foreign-cash declaration mirror of inbound.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: Argentina does not have one simple symmetric cash-declaration figure. Three distinct border regimes under ARCA RG 5659/2025 must not be collapsed: (1) inbound — mandatory OM 2249-A written Customs declaration when cash + bearer instruments (foreign or ARS) + minted precious metals total ≥ USD 10,000 equivalent (declaration trigger, not import ceiling); (2) outbound foreign-currency cash / foreign bearer instruments / minted precious metals — physical baggage carriage only when total < USD 10,000; at ≥ USD 10,000 exit must be through SEFyC-authorised entities (not an ordinary traveller declaration path); (3) outbound ARS cash / ARS bearer instruments — at ≥ USD 10,000 equivalent, OM 2250-B Customs declaration. Per-traveller computation; 50% for under-16 non-emancipated minors; transit exception under Art. 9. ARCA traveller help pages are operational corroboration only; RG 5659 is the controlling legal text where wording differs.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Under the current BCRA Exterior y Cambios official summary, resident natural persons (personas humanas residentes) may access the FX market without an amount ceiling to form external assets in foreign-currency bills or deposits when the operation is effected by debit to an account at a local financial entity. Comunicación A 8226 (April 2025 Phase-3 liberalisation package) likewise permits resident natural-person purchases of foreign-currency bills for holding or deposit constitution without prior BCRA conformity when (among other conditions) the operation is debited from a local financial-entity account, or local-currency cash use does not exceed the equivalent of USD 100 in the calendar month across entities/concepts, with registration and income/asset-consistency evidence. Formation of external assets under other modalities, family remittances and certain derivatives remain subject to monthly limits/conditions on the BCRA summary. Purchase/holding access is not unrestricted outward transfer. Distinct post-A 8307 securities overlays apply and must not be collapsed: Comunicación A 8332 first incorporated punto 3.8.5 requiring a client sworn undertaking not to purchase securities with foreign-currency settlement from access and for the following 90 calendar days, initially for specified financial/FX-entity insiders and related persons (significant shareholders, directors, síndicos, senior managers, FX-entity equivalents, and close family). Comunicación A 8336 replaced that 3.8.5 text so the same 90-day undertaking applies in all cases for the relevant resident-natural-person access path. Separately, Comunicación A 8417 point 7 (effective 10 April 2026) requires, for outward transfers under TO punto 3.14.1, online BCRA registration when that system is operative plus a client sworn declaration not to purchase securities with foreign-currency settlement for the following 90 calendar days, subject to the stated exceptions (primary subscriptions of resident debt held ≥15 business days; reinvestment of Tesoro Nacional / BCRA FX coupons within 15 business days).
rules.non_resident_rules: The current BCRA Exterior y Cambios official summary states that non-residents generally require prior BCRA conformity to operate in the FX market, with enumerated exceptions (including international organisations, diplomatic/consular representations, pension beneficiaries and other listed cases). Portfolio-investment repatriation of capital and income in CNV-authorised locally quoted instruments, certain mutual funds composed of those instruments, and sight/term deposits at local financial entities are among the exceptions identified on that summary. Tourist non-residents may repurchase up to USD 100 where the intervening entity verifies online that they settled an equal or greater amount in the prior 90 calendar days. Comunicación A 8230 and later amendments (including A 8245 / A 8257) create additional transaction-specific repatriation paths for direct and portfolio investment that must not be collapsed into 'non-residents can repatriate freely'; the exact post-A 8307 article pins remain a Pinpoint Hardening residual. Non-resident treatment is concept-specific.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: BCRA Exterior y Cambios rules require FX operations through an authorised FX entity, at a freely agreed exchange rate between the parties, with a purchase/sale boleto as a sworn declaration and documentation sufficient for the entity to verify genuineness and correct concept coding. As a general rule, proceeds from exports of goods and services (and disposal of certain non-produced non-financial assets) must be surrendered/settled in the FX market within BCRA deadlines; financial indebtedness liquidation is a condition for later market access to pay principal/interest. Resident access to pay imports, non-resident services, profits/dividends and financial debt is available when the concept-specific conditions are met. Intra-resident foreign-currency debt payments via the FX market are generally not permitted except for listed exceptions. 2025–2026 CAMEX liberalisations remain concept-specific, not a general 'current account free' claim: A 8226 includes dividend/import-service timing measures, and Comunicación A 8417 further adjusts human-person goods-export liquidation exceptions aligned with the services path, extends the human-person services liquidation exception across service concepts, lengthens selected export-income deadlines, and eases certain debt-related FX-market access paths (including linked financial-debt principal access under stated conditions).
rules.exchange_controls: Argentina's reviewed official sources do not establish a single general foreign-exchange authorisation regime that can be summarised as 'no controls' or as a universal prior-approval system for every transaction. Distinct layers apply and must not be conflated: (i) a BCRA floating-within-bands monetary regime (market determination inside the band; boundary/intervention mechanics) — a monetary fact kept separate from FX-access rules; (ii) Mercado Libre de Cambios operations through authorised entities at freely agreed rates with genuineness/concept documentation; (iii) concept-specific access, surrender/liquidation and reporting rules under the Exterior y Cambios TO through A 8307 plus complementary post-A 8307 CAMEX communications that remain currently operative (including A 8336 securities-settlement undertakings on the resident access path and A 8417 outward-transfer / export-services-debt adjustments); (iv) prior BCRA conformity for categories that still require it (including many non-resident operations and certain resident legal-person external-asset formations), with enumerated exceptions; and (v) Customs-enforced asymmetric physical-cash carriage/declaration rules under ARCA RG 5659/2025. Absence of a located restriction is not evidence that none exists. Provisional exchange-control posture for later Passage Check transcription is capital_account_regulated; exact locator fidelity remains for Pinpoint Hardening.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Practical FX conversion and transfers are effected through BCRA-authorised financial/FX entities. Resident natural-person bill/deposit formation is operationally tied to local-account debit (or the limited local-cash path). Entities must register relevant operations in BCRA online systems where required and obtain documentation supporting genuineness and concept classification. Passenger cash movements at the border are operationally administered by ARCA Customs (OM 2249-A / OM 2250-B) with data supplied to the UIF under RG 5659/2025. Banking/exchange AML obligations for financial and exchange entities are framed by the UIF normative corpus (including Resolución UIF 199/2024 and complementary rules as listed on the UIF vigentes page) as a separate compliance layer from BCRA FX-access eligibility.

disclaimer: This page provides general informational reference only. Argentine foreign-exchange, monetary-regime and passenger cash rules change frequently through BCRA CAMEX communications and ARCA resolutions, and transaction-specific requirements may depend on residency or entity status, documentation, amount, securities interactions and the applicable concept code. The consolidated Exterior y Cambios texto ordenado is not alone a complete statement of current rules. This is not legal, regulatory, tax, financial, or compliance advice. Always verify current rules directly with the BCRA, ARCA / Dirección General de Aduanas, the UIF or an authorised FX entity before making any financial or travel decisions.
